rationale: Tests recall of PCR thermocycling steps, temperatures, and key reagents immediately after the block that completes the molecular diagnostic techniques learning point.
Tests understanding of PCR's inability to distinguish live from dead organisms — a critical clinical limitation highlighted in the clinical pearl that closes this learning point.
Tests visual recognition of organism morphology matched to characteristic staining appearance — the core visual skill introduced in the conventional microscopy methods learning point.

Tests the ability to apply the clinical framework for choosing diagnostic methods — specifically why culture remains essential despite molecular advances — at the block that closes this learning point.
Tests application of the golden rules of specimen collection to a clinical scenario — anchored at the block that closes the general principles learning point.

Tests application of specimen-specific transport rules to CSF — a high-stakes clinical scenario where incorrect handling causes false-negative results — at the block that closes the specimen-specific guidelines learning point.

Tests the ability to analyse epidemiological data (attack rate, epidemic curve, incubation period, secondary transmission) to classify an outbreak — at the block that closes the epidemiology learning point.
Tests understanding of why diagnostic labels on specimen containers violate professional principles — anchored at the block that closes the respectful specimen handling learning point.

Tests application of effective communication principles to a realistic specimen collection scenario involving patient literacy — anchored at the block that closes the communication skills learning point.

Tests application of confidentiality principles and Indian legal framework to a realistic scenario where a third party demands patient results — anchored at the block that closes the confidentiality learning point.
